The Huracán was succeeded by the [[Lamborghini Temerario|Temerario]], announced in 2024. ==Name== [[File:Lamborghini Huracán - logo (Italy, 2014).svg|thumb|Logo]] The Huracán's name (''huracán'' being the Spanish word for hurricane) is inspired by a [[Spanish fighting bull]]. Historic Spanish fighting bulls have traditionally provided the names of most Lamborghini car models. Huracán was a bull known for its courage that fought in 1879.{{cite web|last=Frank|first=Robert|title=Lamborghini's Huracan: A new weapon in the supercar wars|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2013/12/20/lamborghinis-huracan-a-new-weapon-in-the-supercar-wars.html|work=[[CNBC]]|date=2013-12-20|access-date=2014-02-09}} ==Specifications and performance== ===Specifications=== ====Engine==== The Huracán retains the 5.2-litre [[naturally aspirated engine|naturally aspirated]] [[Lamborghini V10|Audi/Lamborghini V10 engine]] of the facelifted [[Lamborghini Gallardo|Gallardo]], tuned to generate a maximum power output of {{convert|610|PS|kW hp PS|0|abbr=on|order=out}}.{{Citation needed|date=May 2024}} To ensure its balance and performance, the car is [[mid-engined]]. The engine has both [[direct fuel injection]] and [[multi-point fuel injection]]. It combines the benefits of both systems; it is the first time this combination has been used in a [[V10 engine]]. The [[firing order]] of the engine is 1, 6, 5, 10, 2, 7, 3, 8, 4, 9. This is printed on a metal plate on the top of the engine, as with all other Lamborghini models. The transmission performs differently depending on the mode the driver has selected. The different drive modes available are Sport, Strada and Corsa, Corsa being the highest performance mode.{{cite web|title=Huracan LP 610-4|url=http://www.lamborghini.com/en/models/huracan-lp-610-4/explore/|publisher=[[Lamborghini]]|access-date=9 February 2014|archive-date=22 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150222015022/http://www.lamborghini.com/en/models/huracan-lp-610-4/explore/|url-status=dead}} The Huracán will only be available with an automatic transmission; a manual will not be offered.{{cite web|last=Stoklosa|first=Alexander|title=2014 Lamborghini Huracán LP 610-4: Succeeding Supercar Ubiquity|date=20 December 2013|url= http://www.caranddriver.com/news/2014-lamborghini-huracan-lp-610-4-photos-and-info-news |publisher=[[Car and Driver]]|access-date=19 February 2014}} The Huracán also has a [[magnetically controlled suspension]] system. It utilises [[magnetorheological damper]]s to very quickly change how the suspension acts, ensuring performance as well as usability. The Huracán has various components in common with the second generation of the [[Audi R8]]. This is due to the sharing of Volkswagen's sports car technology among both of the cars. ===Interior=== [[File:Lamborghini_Huracan_Interior.jpg|thumbnail|right|Interior]] The Huracán has various interior options for upgraded comfort inside the car. It has a choice for full electric control and heating of the sport seats in addition to the standard lengthwise alignment and electric backrest. The car also has an optional navigation system and leather upholstering. The Huracán is one of the first sports cars moving the infotainment system out of the center stack: Lamborghini Infotainment System. The result: a display that lets the driver decide what they want to see. It is the first Lamborghini automobile to use the 12.3 inch [[Thin-film-transistor liquid-crystal display|TFT]] [[Audi virtual cockpit|virtual cockpit]] from parent company [[Audi]],{{cite news |url=http://jalopnik.com/the-lamborghini-huracan-is-the-real-first-use-of-audis-1570346055 |title=The Lamborghini Huracan Is The Real First Use Of Audi's Virtual Cockpit |first=Travis |last=Okulski |work=Jalopnik |date=1 May 2014 |access-date=14 January 2015}} which is available with high-definition (1440 x 540{{cite news |url=http://techgage.com/news/lamborghinis-newest-supercar-is-equipped-with-nvidias-tegra-3-tech/ |title=Lamborghini's Newest Supercar is Equipped with NVIDIA's Tegra 3 Tech |work=Techgage |first=J.D. |last=Kane |date=5 March 2014 |access-date=14 January 2015}}) [[3D computer graphics]], [[Bluetooth]], [[Google Earth]] [[Automotive navigation system|GPS navigation]] and [[Multi Media Interface]]-like menu and dashboard controls, all powered by [[Nvidia]] [[Tegra 3]]. ===Technology=== Various aspects of the Huracán are technologically advanced. The car has full [[LED headlamp]]s, which ensure higher contrast in night conditions. Also, the Huracán has optional "Lamborghini Dynamic Steering" (LDS) to add to the standard power steering. The Dynamic Steering changes the steering performance from normal, comfortable steering to a racing feeling. The main control for changing the car's performance according to driving conditions is the mode selector ANIMA (Adaptive Network Intelligent Management). ANIMA controls the engine, the transmission, LDS, the all-wheel drive, magnetorheological suspension, and the [[electronic stability control]]. The Lamborghini Piattaforma Inerziale (LPI) carries out precise measurements of the vehicle movements using on board sensors (3 [[accelerometer]]s and 3 [[gyroscope]]s) linked to ANIMA via high-speed [[FlexRay]] [[CAN bus]].{{cite news |url=http://www.netcarshow.com/lamborghini/2015-huracan_lp610-4/ |title=Lamborghini Huracan LP610-4 (2015) |access-date=14 January 2015}} The driver can select street, sport, or race mode to alter how systems like the engine or transmission respond while driving. == Huracán (2014–2019) == === Huracán LP 610-4 Coupé (2014–2019) === The LP 610-4 designation comes from the car having 610 metric horsepower and four-wheel drive, while LP stands for "Longitudinale Posteriore", which refers to the longitudinal mid-rear engine position. Autos |date=18 November 2015 |access-date=1 December 2015}} === Huracán LP 580-2 Spyder (2016–2019) === [[File:WMC P JAIA17 Lamborghini Huracán LP 580-2 RWD Spyder 1.jpg|thumb|left|Lamborghini Huracán LP580-2 Spyder]] A convertible variant of the Huracán LP 580-2 was unveiled at the [[Los Angeles Auto Show#2016|Los Angeles Auto Show]] on 16 November 2016. The 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 engine is the same as in the coupé, and generates a maximum power output of {{convert|580|PS|kW hp PS|0|abbr=on|order=out}}. ''[[Motor Trend]]'' recorded a 0-60 mph (97 km/h) time of 3.2 seconds, and the top speed is {{convert|199|mph|km/h|0|abbr=on|order=flip}}.{{Cite web |date=2017-10-23 |title=The Last True Supercar: Lamborghini Huracán LP580-2 Spyder |url=https://www.motortrend.com/reviews/lamborghini-huracan-lp580-2-spyder-review-last-true-supercar |access-date=2025-07-31 |website=MotorTrend |language=en}} {{anchor|LP 640-4 Performante}} === Huracán LP 640-4 Performante (2017–2019) === {{Multiple image | image1 = 2018 Lamborghini Huracan Performante 2.jpg | image2 = 2018 Lamborghini Huracan Performante 4.jpg | direction = vertical | align = | caption1 = Lamborghini Huracán Performante front view | caption2 = Lamborghini Huracán Performante rear view }} A track oriented variant of the Huracán, called the Performante, was unveiled at the [[Geneva Motor Show#2017|2017 Geneva Motor Show]].{{cite news |url=http://www.autoblog.com/2017/03/06/lamborghini-huracan-performante-revealed-geneva/ |title=This is the fully uncovered Lamborghini Huracán Performante |first=Joel |last=Stocksdale |work=AutoBlog |date=6 March 2017 |access-date=6 March 2017}}{{cite news |url=http://www.firstpost.com/auto/2017-geneva-motor-show-lamborghini-to-showcase-huracan-performante-3221400.html |title=2017 Geneva Motor Show: Lamborghini to showcase Huracan Performante |work=FirstPost |date=26 January 2017 |access-date=4 March 2017}} The Performante underwent various exterior changes with the most noticeable being the front and rear bumpers. Carbon fibre is used for the bumpers and the side skirts. An adjustable carbon fibre rear wing has been added to increase downforce. The position of the exhaust has also been changed, and is now just a bit above the rear diffuser. The interior also underwent noticeable changes, now sporting new seats and a new digital speedometer (similar to that of the [[Lamborghini Aventador#Aventador LP 750-4 SuperVeloce|Aventador SV]]'s speedometer).{{cite news |url=http://www.caradvice.com.au/530002/2017-lamborghini-huracan-performante-revealed-coming-to-australia-in-winter/ |title=Lamborghini Huracán Performante revealed, coming to Australia in winter |first=Derek |last=Fung |work=Car Advice |location=Australia |date=6 March 2017|access-date=6 March 2017}} The Performante's 5.2-litre V10 has been tuned to have a power output of {{convert|640|PS|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} at 8,000 rpm and {{convert|443|lbft|Nm|abbr=on|0|order=flip}} of torque at 6,500 rpm. The weight has also decreased by {{convert|40|kg|lbs|abbr=on}}, courtesy of the forged aluminium and forged carbon fibre body components (first used in the construction of the [[Lamborghini Sesto Elemento|Sesto Elemento]]). All the new aero components on the car have active aerodynamic capability and help keep the car stable at high speeds. The Performante is capable of accelerating from {{cvt|0-100|km/h|mph|0|abbr=on}} in 2.9 seconds, {{cvt|0-200|km/h|mph|0|abbr=on}} in 8.9 seconds. It also has a theoretical top speed of {{convert|325|km/h|mph|abbr=on|round=5}}. The car has been stiffened by 10% with new springs, roll bars, and radial axial arm bushings. The [[Magnetorheological damper|magnetorheological suspension]] has been reworked to give a driver a serious track experience. The Lamborghini Dynamic Steering has been re-calibrated. The Performante utilises Lamborghini's new ALA (Aerodinamica Lamborghini Attiva) system, which is said to be 80% lighter than regular sports car hydraulic systems. According to Lamborghini, ALA is also said to provide 750% more downforce than the standard Huracán.{{cite news |url=http://www.motortrend.com/news/lamborghini-unveils-ring-master-huracan-performante/ |title=Lamborghini Huracan Performante Revealed, Delivers 640 HP |first=Jonathon |last=Klein |work=MotorTrend |location=USA |date=6 March 2017 |access-date=7 March 2017}} {{anchor|LP 640-4 Performante Spyder}} ===Huracán LP 640-4 Performante Spyder (2018–2019)=== [[File:Dealer plate FL 128 U detail (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|Lamborghini Huracán Performante Spyder]] The Lamborghini Huracán Performante Spyder was unveiled at the [[Geneva Motor Show#2018|2018 Geneva Motor Show]]. It takes much of the styling inspiration from the coupé and the outgoing LP 610-4 Spyder. The Spyder is identical to the coupé from performance and technological standpoint, but the acceleration time from {{cvt|0-60|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} has risen by one-tenth of a second and stands at 3.1 seconds while the {{cvt|0-124|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} has risen by four-tenths of a second and stands at 9.3 seconds. Due to the loss of the roof, the Spyder weighs {{cvt|125|kg|lb|0|abbr=on}} more than the coupé due to chassis reinforcing components. Top speed remains the same as well and stands at {{cvt|202|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}}. Deliveries of the Spyder began in the fourth quarter of 2018.{{cite press release |url=http://www.evo.co.uk/news/19503/lamborghini-huracan-performante-spyder-unveiled-at-2018-geneva-motor-show |title=Lamborghini Huracán Performante Spyder revealed at the 2018 Geneva Motor Show |first=Adam |last=Towler |work=Evo magazine |date=6 March 2018 |access-date=14 March 2018}} == Facelift (2019–2024) == === Huracán LP 640-4 Evo (2019–2024) === [[File:2022 Lamborghini Huracan EVO Orange.jpg|thumb|Lamborghini Huracán Evo front view]] The Huracán received a mid-cycle update in 2019, now being called the Huracán Evo.{{cite web|url=https://www.evo.co.uk/lamborghini/huracan/22109/lamborghini-huracan-evo-revealed-updated-junior-supercar-to-fight-mclaren|title=Lamborghini Huracan EVO revealed – updated junior supercar to fight McLaren 570S|date=7 January 2019|first=Jordan|last=Katsianis|publisher=[[Evo (magazine)|Evo]]|access-date=9 February 2019}} It now shares its engine and some of the technology with the Performante variant. The updated version of the Huracán has a more aggressive design language, the new front bumper has integrated aeroblades for improved downforce along with the rear styling inspired by the Performante variant, having the same rear diffuser, exhaust pipe position and radiators. A new ducktail spoiler improves downforce by 5 times as compared to the outgoing model. The engine is shared with the Performante and generates {{cvt|640|PS|kW hp PS|0|abbr=on|order=out}} at 8,000 rpm and {{cvt|443|lbft|Nm|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} of torque at 6,500 rpm. The exhaust system is more refined and has titanium intake valves. This allows the car to achieve a {{cvt|0-97|kph|mph|0|abbr=on}}acceleration time of 2.9 seconds, {{cvt|0-124|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} acceleration time of 9 seconds and a top speed of {{cvt|325|kph|mph|0|abbr=on}}. The car has a braking distance from {{cvt|100-0|kph|mph|0|abbr=on}} of {{cvt|104|ft|m|0|abbr=on}}. The Huracán Evo has a rear-wheel steering system for improved handling and a torque vectoring system. A new central processing unit controls the various functions of the car and monitors various settings. The control system is controlled by the new infotainment system (via an 8.4 inch touchscreen) dubbed the ''Lamborghini Dinamica Veicolo Integrata'' which has integrated both [[Apple CarPlay]] and [[Android Auto]]. The infotainment system predicts the driving modes by a ''feed forward logic''.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} The feed forward logic works by sensors monitoring the lateral, longitudinal and vertical accelerations, as well as roll, pitch and yaw rate to predict the best possible driving mode for the driver. The magnetorheological suspension is also revised and now uses electromagnetic current to adjust the suspension system in accordance with the driving mode.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} The transmission system from the outgoing model is retained which transfers power to all four wheels. A new ''Ego'' mode allows the driver to change driving settings to their own preference.{{cite news |url=https://carbuzz.com/news/say-hello-to-the-new-lamborghini-huracan-evo |title=Say Hello To The New Lamborghini Huracan Evo |first=Martin |last=Bigger|work=Carbuzz |date=7 January 2019 |access-date=7 January 2019}}{{cite news |url=https://www.topgear.com/car-news/supercars/new-lamborghini-huracan-evo |title=This is the new Lamborghini Huracán Evo |first=Ollie| last=Kew |work=[[Top Gear (2002 TV series)|Top Gear]] |date=7 January 2019 |access-date=7 January 2019}} === Huracán LP 640-4 Evo Spyder (2019–2024) === [[File:Lamborghini Huracan Evo Spyder Genf 2019 1Y7A5557.jpg|thumb|2019 Lamborghini Huracan Evo Spyder rear view]] The Huracán Evo Spyder was introduced online in February 2019. The Spyder has the same enhancements as the coupé but is {{cvt|100|kg|lb|0|abbr=on}} heavier due to the addition of chassis reinforcement components owing to the loss of the roof. The car has the same canvas folding soft top as the outgoing model which takes 17 seconds for operation and is operable at speeds up to {{cvt|31|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}}. The Spyder can accelerate to {{cvt|100|kph|mph|0|abbr=on}} in 3.1 seconds from a standstill, to {{cvt|124|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} in 9.3 seconds and can attain a top speed of {{cvt|202|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}}.{{cite news |url=https://www.topgear.com/car-news/geneva-motor-show/lamborghini-huracan-evo-now-available-minus-roof |title=The Lamborghini Huracán Evo: now available minus a roof |first=Ollie |last=Kew |work=[[Top Gear (magazine)|Top Gear]] |location=UK |date=26 February 2019 |access-date=26 February 2019}}{{cite news |url=https://www.cnet.com/roadshow/news/lamborghini-huracan-evo-spyder-geneva-motor-show/ |title=Lamborghini Huracan Evo Spyder revealed ahead of Geneva Motor Show |first=Jake |last=Holmes |work=[[CNET]] |location=US |date=5 March 2019 |access-date=19 March 2019}} === Huracán LP 610-2 Evo RWD (2020–2024) === [[File:2020 Lamborghini Huracan EVO RWD.jpg|thumb|Lamborghini Huracán Evo RWD front view]] A rear-wheel drive variant of the Evo debuted in January 2020, replacing the LP 580–2. The front splitter has been reshaped and generates more airflow, which is directed to the revised diffuser. Unique to the RWD model is P-TCS (Performance Traction Control System) that ensures that torque is not cut off abruptly; Lamborghini claims this increases oversteer by 30 percent compared to the LP 580–2. The engine is detuned and is now rated at {{cvt|610|PS|kW hp PS|0|abbr=on|order=out}}. Due to the detuned engine, the car is slower than the standard Huracán Evo accelerating to {{convert|100|kph|mph|abbr=on}} in 3.3 seconds while having the same top speed. The car also receives a unique paint option, Giallo Belenus, along with a matching interior upholstered in leather and microsuede.{{Cite web|url=https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a30397903/lamborghini-huracan-evo-2020-rear-wheel-drive/|title=2020 Lamborghini Huracán Evo, Now with 30 Percent More Oversteer|work=[[Car and Driver]]|last=Atiyeh|first=Clifford|date=4 January 2020|access-date=5 January 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.roadandtrack.com/new-cars/a30415618/2021-lamborghini-huracan-evo-rear-wheel-drive-pictures-specs-info/|title=You Can Now Get the Lamborghini Huracán Evo in Rear-Wheel Drive|date=6 January 2020|first=Brian|last=Silvestro|work=Road & Track |publisher=[[Road & Track]]|access-date=11 January 2020}} === Huracán LP 610-2 Evo RWD Spyder (2020–2024) === A convertible version of the rear-wheel drive variant of the Evo was showcased in May 2020, replacing the LP 580-2 Spyder. Like the Coupé variant, the convertible has a power output of {{cvt|610|PS|kW hp PS|0|abbr=on|order=out}}. The convertible has a {{cvt|0-97|kph|mph|0|abbr=on}} acceleration time of 3.5 seconds and has a claimed top speed of {{cvt|201|mph|kph|0|abbr=on|order=flip}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a32404225/lamborghini-huracan-evo-spyder-rwd-photos-info/|title=602-HP Lamborghini Huracán Evo RWD Now Available as Spyder Droptop|work=[[Car and Driver]]|last=Hoffman|first=Connor|date=7 May 2020|access-date=8 May 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.autocar.co.uk/car-news/new-cars/new-lamborghini-huracan-evo-rwd-spyder-revealed|title= New Lamborghini Huracan Evo RWD Spyder revealed |date=7 May 2020|first=Felix|last=Page|work=[[Autocar (magazine)|Autocar]]|publisher=[[Haymarket Media Group]]|access-date=8 May 2020}} === Huracán LP 640-2 STO (2021–2024) === {{Multiple image |image2= 2022 Lamborghini Huracan STO Rear.jpg |image1= 2021 Lamborghini Huracan STO Blue.jpg |caption2= Huracán STO }} The Huracán STO (Super Trofeo Omologato) is a track focused variant of the Huracán. The STO has a taller rear wing with a roof snorkel for engine cooling. There is a shark fin aerodynamic device connecting the roof snorkel with the rear wing. The engine cover is reminiscent of the Lamborghini Super Trofeo Evo race cars. The entire hood opens to reveal a small compartment for storing racing equipment and the body is made of 75% carbon fibre. The engine and the power output of the STO is the same as the Huracán Performante and the Huracán Evo and it has rear-wheel drive with a rear wheel steering system and CCMR brakes inspired from Formula 1. The STO comes with three new driving modes: STO for road driving, TROFEO for fast lap times on dry tarmac, and PIOGGIA for wet weather driving. The bucket seats on the interior feature [[racing harness]]es. === Huracán LP 640-2 Tecnica (2022–2024) === [[File:2022 Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica (cropped).jpg|thumb|Huracán Tecnica]] Unveiled on April 12, 2022, The Huracán Tecnica sits between the EVO RWD and the track-focused STO.{{cite news |url=https://paultan.org/2022/04/13/lamborghini-huracan-tecnica-debuts/ |title=Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica debuts with STO's 5.2L V10 – 640 PS, 565 Nm; 0-100 km/h in 3.2s; 325 km/h |first=Gerard |last=Lye |work=paultan.org |location=Malaysia |date=2022-04-13 |access-date=2022-05-24}} It is {{cvt|6.1|cm}} longer than the EVO, but is the same height and width. It uses the naturally aspirated V10 engine from the STO and has a top speed of {{cvt|325|km/h}} and an acceleration time of {{cvt|0–100|km/h}} in 3.2 seconds.{{Cite web |first=Brandon | last = Livesay |date=2022-04-12 |title=There's a new Lamborghini, see all the pics of the Huracán Tecnica |url=https://supercarblondie.com/lamborghini-new-huracan-tecnica-photos-specs-details-updates/ |access-date=2022-04-12 |website=Supercar Blondie - Automotive, Gaming, Tech, Lifestyle, Watches |language=en-US}} According to Lamborghini, the Tecnica's aerodynamic changes increase downforce by 35 percent and reduce drag by 20 percent compared to the EVO.{{Cite web |last=Gilboy |first=James |date=2022-04-12 |title=The 631-HP Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica Turns Up Downforce But Not Drag |url=https://www.thedrive.com/news/the-631-hp-lamborghini-huracan-tecnica-turns-up-downforce-but-not-drag |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=The Drive |language=en}} === Huracán LP 610-4 Sterrato (2023–2024) === [[File:2023 Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato Yellow.jpg|thumb|Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato]] [[File:Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato 1X7A1622.jpg|thumb|Lamborghini Huracán Sterrato rear view]] In June 2019, Lamborghini introduced an off-road concept sports car based on the Huracán Evo called the Huracán Sterrato.{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J8obUT0TXR4 |title=La fine del folle V10 Lambo {{!}} Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato |trans-title=The end of the crazy V10 Lambo {{!}} Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato |publisher=Drive Zone Italia |date=2024-11-30 |access-date=2025-10-12 |via=Italia}} The ground clearance of the car was increased by {{cvt|47|mm|in|0|abbr=on}} with the car's front approach improved by 1% and the departure angle enhanced by 6.5%. Super Trofeo EVO}} === Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo (2014–2019) === [[File:Nicola Larini, Petri Corse Lamborghini Huracan LP 620-2 Super Trofeo, 2016 Lamborghini Blancpain Super Trofeo Series R4, The 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 now generates {{convert|612|hp|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} and {{convert|570|Nm|lbft|0|abbr=on}} of torque.{{cite web|title=Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo|url=http://www.lamborghini.com/en/models/huracan-super-trofeo/overview/|access-date=14 January 2015|publisher=Lamborghini|archive-date=6 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106005529/http://www.lamborghini.com/en/models/huracan-super-trofeo/overview|url-status=dead}} The vehicle was unveiled at the [[ACI Vallelunga Circuit]].{{cite news|url=http://www.autoblog.com/2014/07/17/lamborghini-huracan-lp610-4-super-trofeo-teaser/|title=Lamborghini previews new Huracán Super Trofeo|last=Joseph|first=Noah|date=17 July 2014|work=autoblog.com|access-date=23 August 2014}} ===Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo EVO (2019–present)=== [[File:24H Series 2022 Spa Nr. 720.jpg|thumb|The No. 720 Huracán Super Trofeo EVO of RD Signs - Siauliai competing in the [[12 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps|2022 12 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps]].]] The Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo EVO is the successor to the Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo. The 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 has the same power and torque, respectively {{convert|612|hp|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} and {{convert|570|Nm|lbft|0|abbr=on}} of torque. ==== Huracán Super Trofeo EVO Collector's Edition ==== The Huracán Super Trofeo EVO Collector's Edition is a limited-run version of the Huracán Super Trofeo EVO. The unique colour theme is done so in collaboration with Roger DuBuis, a famous watchmaker. The car now generates a little over {{convert|621|hp|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} from the 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 with torque remaining the same as the standard car. The bodywork was changed with the introduction of a roof scoop and a new roll cage design with the ability to extract a driver out from the top.{{Cite web|last1=Mihalascu |first1=Dan |date=2019-03-11|title=Lamborghini Drops Watch-Themed Huracan Super Trofeo Evo Collector 2019 Edition|url=https://www.carscoops.com/2019/03/lamborghini-drops-watch-themed-huracan-super-trofeo-evo-collector-2019-edition/|access-date=2020-08-01|website=Carscoops|language=en-US}} ===Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo EVO2 (2022–present)=== [[File:Lamborghini Super Trofeo Europe 2024 Spa-Francorchamps VSR Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO2 No.95 Baptiste Moulin (DSC07604).jpg|thumb|The No. 95 Huracán Super Trofeo EVO2 of VSR competing at [[Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps]].]] The Huracán LP 620-2 Super Trofeo EVO2 was announced in May 2021. It features major aerodynamic refinements and more powerful brakes over the Super Trofeo EVO. Its front end has been redesigned with new headlights, air curtains on both sides of the bumper, and a reshaped splitter made with carbon fibre. In the rear, the LED lights are thinner and the diffuser is bigger. The rocker panel extensions and some of the aerodynamic elements fitted to the rear end are now made with the lightweight material rather than with plastic. Lamborghini's Squadra Corsa division developed a new braking system in-house featuring bigger brake rotors and redesigned calipers capable of housing larger brake pads. Power and torque does not change however, remaining at {{convert|612|hp|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} and {{convert|570|Nm|lbft|0|abbr=on}} of torque. Teams racing a Super Trofeo EVO will be able to purchase an upgrade kit to bring their car to EVO2 specifications.{{Cite web |title=Lamborghini Huracán EVO2 race car is a harbinger of future models |url=https://www.autoblog.com/2021/05/26/2022-lamborghini-huracan-evo2-race-car/ |access-date=2023-01-30 |website=Autoblog |date=26 May 2021 |language=en}}{{citation needed|date=October 2022}}{{clarify|reason=Used to say 2021. WP uses calendar years.|date=October 2022}} ===Huracán GT3 (2015–2019)=== Introduced in 2015, The Lamborghini Huracán GT3 was developed in collaboration with Dallara. It features the 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 engine of the standard car with {{convert|520|hp|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} and {{convert|510|Nm|lbft|0|abbr=on}} of torque and has a weight of {{cvt|1230|kg|lb|0|abbr=on}}. It debuted in the [[2015 Blancpain GT Series]] Endurance Cup race held in [[Monza Circuit|Monza]] and secured an impressive win in its first competitive outing with [[Grasser Racing Team]]. [[Team Lazarus]] won the [[2016 International GT Open]] with drivers [[Thomas Biagi]] and [[Fabrizio Crestani]]. Also, Barwell Motorsport claimed four wins in the [[2016 British GT Championship]] and won the Teams' Championship in [[2017 British GT Championship|2017]], [[Grasser Racing Team]] won a race at the [[2016 ADAC GT Masters]], and [[Paul Miller Racing]] won a race in the GTD class at [[2016 Oak Tree Grand Prix|2016 Michelin GT Challenge at VIR]]. [[File:Daytona 24 2017 11 Grasser Lamborghini Hurac GT3.jpg|thumb|right|The No. 11 Huracán GT3 of [[GRT Grasser Racing Team]] during the [[2017 24 Hours of Daytona]].]] The [[2017 Blancpain GT Series]] was also won by [[Grasser Racing Team]] with factory drivers [[Andrea Caldarelli]], [[Mirko Bortolotti]] and [[Christian Engelhart]]. The #63 Huracán GT3 driven by them took overall victories in the Endurance Cup races at [[Monza Circuit|Monza]] and [[Silverstone Circuit|Silverstone]] and a Sprint Cup race held at [[Brands Hatch]]. [[FFF Racing Team]] won the [[2018 Blancpain GT Series Asia]] with [[Martin Kodrić]] and [[Dennis Lind]]. On 28 January 2018 on the first race of the [[2018 WeatherTech SportsCar Championship]], the {{abbr|No.|Number}} 11 Lamborghini Huracán GT3 of Grasser Racing Team finished first at the [[2018 24 Hours of Daytona]] in the [[Group GT3|GTD]] class. It was the first time that Lamborghini has won a 24-hour race in history. The {{abbr|No.|Number}} 48 Huracán of [[Paul Miller Racing]] went on to win the drivers, teams, and manufacturers championships for Lamborghini.{{cite news |url=https://racer.com/2018/10/15/amazing-finish-nets-gtd-crowns-for-sellers-snow-and-lamborghini/ |title='Amazing' finish nets GTD crowns for Sellers, Snow and Lamborghini |work=Racer |location=US |date=15 October 2018 |access-date=31 October 2018}} === Huracán GT3 Evo (2019–2022) === [[File:Miguel Ramos, Barwell Motorsport Lamborghini Huracan GT3 Evo, 2019.jpg|thumb|right|The No. 77 Barwell Motorsport Huracán GT3 Evo competing in the [[2019 Blancpain GT Series Endurance Cup|2019 3 Hours of Silverstone]].]] The Huracán GT3 Evo is the successor to the Huracán GT3. It features the upgraded 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 engine, now with {{convert|580|hp|kW hp PS|abbr=on|0|order=out}} and {{convert|488|Nm|lbft|0|abbr=on}} of torque and has a slightly reduced weight of {{cvt|1229.4|kg|lb|0|abbr=on}}. It made its racing debut in the [[2019 24 Hours of Daytona]], the opening round of the [[2019 WeatherTech SportsCar Championship]], where it took the [[Group GT3|GTD]] class victory for a second time with Grasser Racing Team. The #11 Huracán GT3 Evo was driven by [[Mirko Bortolotti]], Rik Breukers, [[Christian Engelhart]] and Rolf Ineichen. The same car also won the GTD class in the [[2019 12 Hours of Sebring]], which was the second race of the 2019 WeatherTech SportsCar Championship, while another Huracán GT3 Evo from [[Magnus Racing]] took second place. In the 11th round at [[WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca|Laguna Seca]], the #48 Huracán GT3 Evo of [[Paul Miller Racing]] took victory in the GTD class. [[FFF Racing Team]] won the overall [[2019 Blancpain GT Series]] Championship with support from Lamborghini Squadra Corse, with drivers [[Andrea Caldarelli]] and [[Marco Mapelli]] securing Lamborghini's second overall championship in the series in three seasons.{{Cite web |title=FFF Lamborghini pair steal Blancpain Endurance title |url=https://www.motorsport.com/gtwce-endurance/news/blancpain-barcelona-lamborghini-caldarelli-mapelli/4550042/ |access-date=2022-12-16 |website=www.motorsport.com |language=en}} ===Huracán GT3 Evo 2 (2023–2026)=== [[File:2024 24 Hours of Le Mans (54094554888).jpg|thumb|right|The No. 60 Huracán GT3 Evo 2 of [[Iron Lynx]] during the [[2024 24 Hours of Le Mans]].]] In 2022 Lamborghini unveiled the Huracán GT3 Evo 2, which could be purchased as a new car or as an upgrade kit for the previous generation Huracán GT3. The GT3 Evo 2 takes styling cues from the Huracán STO. It features a new intake system and aerodynamic package.{{Cite web |title=Lamborghini Reveal Huracán GT3 Evo 2 {{!}} dailysportscar.com |url=https://www.dailysportscar.com/2022/05/03/lamborghini-reveal-huracan-gt3-evo-2.html |access-date=2022-05-30 |website=www.dailysportscar.com |date=3 May 2022 }} It made its competition debut at the [[2023 24 Hours of Daytona]], where the [[Iron Lynx]] entered #63 Huracán GT3 Evo 2 finished 4th in the GTD Pro class, driven by Lamborghini factory drivers [[Andrea Caldarelli]], [[Mirko Bortolotti]], [[Jordan Pepper]] and [[Romain Grosjean]]. The Huracán GT3 Evo 2 also participated in Lamborghini's debut season in the [[2024 FIA World Endurance Championship]], competing in the [[Group GT3|LMGT3]] class. Two cars were fielded, one by Iron Lynx and another by the all-female [[Iron Dames]] team. The season marked Lamborghini's first entry to the LMGT3 category, which replaced the previous GTE-Am class. Although it was a challenging season overall, the Iron Lynx #19 managed to secure a podium finish in class at [[2024 6 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps|Spa]]. The Iron Dames team achieved two pole positions, including a 4th-place finish in LMGT3 (32nd overall) at the [[2024 24 Hours of Le Mans|24 Hours of Le Mans]]. The new Huracán GT3 Evo 2 had an impressive outing in the [[2023 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters|2023 DTM]] season, where factory driver [[Mirko Bortolotti]], racing for SSR Performance, narrowly missed the championship after securing second place in the drivers' standings, marking Lamborghini's most successful DTM season with five victories since the manufacturer has entered DTM in 2021. Lamborghini's DTM presence expanded from one team with two cars to five cars across two teams in 2023, fielded by SSR Performance and Grasser Racing Team.{{Cite web |date=2023-10-23 |title=Lamborghini brings successful 2023 DTM season to a close at Hockenheim |url=https://www.lamborghini.com/en-en/motorsport/news/lamborghini-brings-successful-2023-dtm-season-to-a-close-at-hockenheim |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=Lamborghini |language=en}} The next season, Mirko Bortolotti was crowned the [[2024 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters|2024 DTM]] champion after finishing second to [[Luca Engstler]] in the season finale at [[Hockenheimring|Hockenheim]]. Bortolotti, driving for SSR Performance, secured the drivers' title for Lamborghini, their first in DTM. For the first time in 31 years, an Italian driver with an Italian brand has won the DTM since [[Nicola Larini]] in 1994 with [[Alfa Romeo]].{{Cite web |date=2024-12-09 |title=Lamborghini creates history as Bortolotti clinches DTM title in Hockenheim season finale |url=https://www.lamborghini.com/en-en/motorsport/news/lamborghini-creates-history-as-bortolotti-clinches-dtm-title-in-hockenheim-season-finale |access-date=2024-12-15 |website=Lamborghini |language=en}} In the [[2024 24 Hours of Spa]], a new all-time GT3 lap record for Spa-Francorchamps was set by factory driver [[Franck Perera]], driving for Grasser Racing Team, clocked a lap time of 2:13.718 during the Superpole session, claiming the pole position for the centenary edition of the race.{{Cite web|title=Race Results 2024 {{!}} CrowdStrike 24 Hours of Spa {{!}} Superpole {{!}} Fanatec GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS Endurance Cup {{!}} Belgium|url=https://www.gt-world-challenge-europe.com/results/2024/crowdstrike-24-hours-of-spa/super-pole|website=GT World Challenge Europe Powered by AWS|access-date=2025-11-28|language=en-GB}} The #163 crew would ultimately finish the race in 5th position overall, completing 478 laps. The next year, on 29 June 2025, Grasser Racing Team achieved a historic milestone with the Huracán GT3 Evo 2 by securing Lamborghini’s first-ever victory in the [[2025 24 Hours of Spa|24 Hours of Spa]]. This victory marked the first overall race win for Lamborghini in a major 24 hour race and also made Lamborghini the 20th different manufacturer to win the Spa 24 Hours.{{Cite news |title=Spa 24 Hours: Lamborghini takes maiden victory |url=https://www.motorsport.com/gtwce-endurance/news/spa-24-hours-lamborghini-takes-maiden-victory/10737727/ |first=Heiko |last=Stritzke |website=motorsport |location=US |date=2025-06-30 |access-date=2025-06-30}} ===Huracán Super Trofeo GT2 (2021–present)=== The Huracán Super Trofeo GT2 was first announced in 2020, making the Super Trofeo eligible for [[SRO GT2|GT2]] competition. Teams who already owned a Huracán Super Trofeo could purchase a kit to convert their car into the GT2 version, allowing for teams to compete in both the Super Trofeo series and the GT2 series using the same chassis. This can be done with all three generations of the Super Trofeo.{{Cite web |last=Lloyd |first=Daniel |title=Lamborghini to Make Huracan Super Trofeo Eligible for GT2 – Sportscar365 |url=https://sportscar365.com/industry/lamborghini-to-make-huracan-super-trofeo-eligible-for-gt2/ |access-date=2022-04-19 |website=sportscar365.com |date=27 October 2020 |language=en-US}} ==Records and controversy== === Nürburgring Nordschleife lap time === In October 2016, a prototype of the Huracán Performante set a lap time of 6:52.01 on the [[Nürburgring Nordschleife]],{{cite AV media |last=Lamborghini |title=Lamborghini Huracán Performante record at the Nürburgring |date=1 March 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ULSUcERlQQ |access-date=12 March 2017}} with [[Marco Mapelli]] behind the wheel, making it one of the world's fastest production cars around the track. This lap was also made on Marco Mapelli's first attempt.{{cite news |url=http://www.express.co.uk/life-style/cars/774720/Lamborghini-Huracan-Performante-Nurburgring-performance-lap-record |title=New Lamborghini Huracan – You won't believe what this super car has just done |first=Luke John |last=Smith |work=Express |location=UK |date=3 March 2017 |access-date=4 March 2017}} However, some critics have stated complaints around the car's lap time, from the official video being sped up to make the lap believable, to the speeds displayed in the video being false{{cite web |url=http://gtspirit.com/2017/03/03/something-isnt-right-lamborghinis-nurburgring-record-video/ |title=Something Isn't Right with the Lamborghini Huracan Performante Nurburgring Record Video |first=Des |last=Sellmeyer |work=GT Spirit |date=3 March 2017 |access-date=4 March 2017}}{{cite web |url=http://www.bridgetogantry.com/blog-did-lambo-fake-that-laptime/ |title=Blog: Did Lambo "fake" that laptime? |work=Bridge To Gantry |date=3 March 2017 |access-date=4 March 2017}} or that it did not use road tires.{{cite AV media|last=Roadshow |title=Jim Glickenhaus is cynical of Lamborghini Performante record |date=8 March 2017|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b2M8zj9PCyA |access-date=26 March 2017}} Lamborghini countered these doubts by sharing telemetry data, and claiming that the car used Pirelli P Zero Trofeo R tires, which were also specified for customer cars. It attributed the record to its Aerodinamica Lamborghini Attiva (ALA) active aerodynamic system ''[[Road & Track]]''. Máté Petrány of ''Road & Track'' had met with lead engineer of Lamborghini, [[Maurizio Reggiani]], to ask about the lap. It was then revealed by Reggiani that the Performante's active aerodynamic system called ''Aerodinamica Lamborghini Attiva'' gives the car the greatest improvement in lap time. An important issue is the spoilers snapping into their lowest-drag setting when the Performante is aimed forward, which results in the removal of acceleration impediment that big aero causes.{{Cite Proved Itself|date=10 March 2017|work=Road & Track|access-date=12 March 2017|language=en}} The Huracán Performante's lap time was beaten by the [[Porsche 991 GT2 RS]] which set a lap time of 6:47.3 in extract: The Lamborghini Huracán (Spanish for "hurricane"; [uɾaˈkan]) is a mid-engine, two-seater sports car made by Lamborghini from 2014 to 2024. Revealed online in December 2013, the Huracán made its worldwide debut at the 2014 Geneva Auto Show and was released to the market in the second quarter of 2014, replacing the Gallardo. The Huracán was succeeded by the Temerario, announced in 2024.
